summary: This paper resolves the open problem posed by Pinzon et al. regarding the extension of 1-joined path graph adjacency determinant monoids to general trees and forests. The author establishes four machine-checked structural theorems: (1) the complete 13-element monoid closure and Green's eggbox structure; (2) the Universal Tree Collapse and Surjectivity Theorem, proving all finite trees collapse into M13 and surject onto all 13 elements; (3) the Exact Cycle-Escape Theorem, showing that adjoining a single cycle breaks finite closure into linear or exponential growth; and (4) comprehensive chain audits correcting minor literature typos. All results are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 (0 sorry) and certified via fraction-free Bareiss arithmetic.
strengths: Complete machine-checked formalization in Lean 4.36.0 with zero 'sorry' statements and zero use of Classical.choice.
Exhaustive computational audit covering all 1,441 labeled trees on 2 <= n <= 6 vertices via Prüfer codes and fraction-free Bareiss elimination.
Sharp structural delineation between tree-induced monoid collapse (|det| <= 1) and cyclic escape leading to unipotent Jordan and exponential determinant growth.
Meticulous verification suite backed by 16 canonical SHA-256 certificates and 61 adversarial pytest checks.
weaknesses: The scope is highly specialized within algebraic graph theory and finite semigroup theory, though its methodological combination of Lean 4 formalization and exact arithmetic certification sets a stellar standard.
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal Tree Collapse and Surjectivity Theorem for 1-joined graph adjacency determinants.
